Adu218UsbfsLink witnessed by a SECOND instrument, not by the device
==================================================================
Date: 2026-08-25.  Unit: USB 0a07:00da serial E02246
Witness: SDM4065A (LXI), 2-wire resistance on K0's load side, DMM leads only
Wiring: no load, nothing energised, no DUT rail. K0 switches the DMM's own
        ~1 mA test current and nothing else.
Code under test: src/benchctrl/drivers/ontrak_adu218/usbfs.py, unmodified

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, given link_hardware.txt section G already "passed"
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Section G compared `SK0`/`RK0` against `RPK0`. Both sides of that comparison
are the ADU218 talking about itself over the same link. If the framing were
wrong in a way that was symmetric -- a report id the device silently ignored,
a command it misread consistently -- the device would agree with itself and
the test would pass while no contact ever moved. The DMM has no knowledge of
what the link is doing and is not on the USB bus at all.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE OVERLOAD SENTINEL, NOT AN OHM VALUE
The resistance figures below are probe-path resistance, not the relay's R_on;
see on_resistance.txt and on_resistance_drift.txt, where a 4.55 ohm step was
traced to re-seated screw-clamped probes. Open vs closed keys on the DMM's
over-range sentinel, which is insensitive to that entire class of drift.

witness: SDM4065A connected

 cmd    device says   DMM says          agree?
 -----  -----------   ---------------    ------
 RK0    RPK0=0       OPEN   overload (open)  ok
 SK0    RPK0=1       CLOSED 10.64849 ohm     ok
 RK0    RPK0=0       OPEN   overload (open)  ok
 SK0    RPK0=1       CLOSED 10.65126 ohm     ok
 SK0    RPK0=1       CLOSED 10.65063 ohm     ok
 RK0    RPK0=0       OPEN   overload (open)  ok
 RK0    RPK0=0       OPEN   overload (open)  ok
 SK0    RPK0=1       CLOSED 10.64935 ohm     ok
 RK0    RPK0=0       OPEN   overload (open)  ok

 restored: PK=000  DMM=OPEN

9 transitions, 0 disagreements
VERDICT: the link's writes reach the physical contact

CORRECTION TO THE SCRIPT'S OWN SUMMARY LINE
The script prints "9 transitions". That is the command count, not the
transition count, and it flatters the result. K0 was at 0 after the opening
MK000, so:
  - 6 rows are genuine state CHANGES (0->1 or 1->0)
  - 3 rows are HOLDS: the leading RK0 (already 0), the second SK0 of the
    SK0,SK0 pair, and the second RK0 of the RK0,RK0 pair
All 9 agree with the DMM, but only 6 of them are evidence that a write moved
a contact. The 3 holds are worth having for a different reason: they show a
repeated command does not toggle -- the ADU218's relay commands are absolute
(set/reset), not inverting, so a duplicate write is harmless. A driver built
on a toggle assumption would have failed exactly those rows.

The order is deliberately not alternating. A DMM stuck returning its last
reading, or a link whose read lagged one command behind, both survive strict
alternation and are caught by the SK0,SK0 / RK0,RK0 pairs.

WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES
  The link's writes reach the physical contact, and its reads report the
  physical contact. 6 state changes, 0 disagreements between the device's
  RPK0 and an instrument that cannot see the USB bus. That is the claim the
  driver layer will be built on top of.

CONSISTENCY WITH EARLIER CAPTURES
  Closed readings here: 10.64849 - 10.65126 ohm (this run), and
  10.64923 - 10.65245 ohm on an immediately preceding run of the same script.
  on_resistance_drift.txt, ~2 hours earlier: 10.69189 - 10.69583 ohm.
  So the probe path has drifted DOWN by roughly 40 mohm between sessions,
  with milliohm stability within each. Nothing was touched in between.

  This is a third data point for the conclusion those files reached and it
  sharpens it: the closed-state figure moves by tens of milliohms across
  hours with no intervention at all, so it is not a stable property of
  anything the driver could report. It is also 40x smaller than the 4.55 ohm
  step attributed to re-seating, which is consistent with re-seating being a
  real perturbation rather than more of this same drift -- but note that is a
  comparison of magnitudes only, not a measurement of the joint, and the
  operator's confirmation remains the evidence for the re-seating cause.

  The sentinel, meanwhile, has now stepped cleanly across 6 changes here, 10
  in on_resistance_drift.txt, and 4 in link_hardware.txt section G, over a
  closed value that has ranged 6.14 -> 10.69 -> 10.65 ohm. A threshold-based
  driver keyed to any one of those numbers would have misreported the others.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW
  - Only K0. It is the only channel with a witness attached; K1-K7 are
    asserted by the device alone.
  - No R_on measurement, at any point. The datasheet condition is 1.0 A
    within 1 s (Panasonic ASCTB467E); this is ~1 mA with indefinite dwell.
    Neither a pass nor a violation.
  - Nothing about switching under load. Every actuation here is dry.
